what_its_for: This medicine is used to treat HIV (Human Immunodeficiency Virus) infection in adults and children who weigh at least 40 kg (about 88 pounds). It contains three antiviral medicines that work together to lower the amount of HIV virus in your blood (called your 'viral load') and help keep your immune system healthy. This medicine does NOT cure HIV, but it helps control the infection and reduces your risk of getting HIV-related illnesses.
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth, exactly as your doctor tells you. Swallow the tablet whole — do not crush, break, or chew it. Take it on an empty stomach, preferably at bedtime. Taking it at bedtime and on an empty stomach helps reduce side effects like dizziness or drowsiness that some people feel, especially in the first few weeks. Try to take it at the same time every day to keep the drug levels steady in your body. Do not stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first, even if you feel well.
dosing: The usual dose for adults and children weighing at least 40 kg is ONE tablet taken once daily. Each tablet contains efavirenz 600 mg, emtricitabine 200 mg, and tenofovir disoproxil fumarate 300 mg. Your doctor will confirm the right dose for you. Do not take more than one tablet per day unless your doctor tells you to.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose and it has been LESS than 12 hours since your scheduled dose time, take it as soon as you remember. If it has been MORE than 12 hours, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at your regular time. Never take two tablets at once to make up for a missed dose. Taking your medicine every day as prescribed is very important — missing doses can allow the virus to become resistant to the medication, making it harder to treat.
storage: Store this medicine at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it in the original container with the lid tightly closed. Store away from heat, light, and moisture — do NOT store in the bathroom. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not use it after the expiration date printed on the bottle. If you need to dispose of unused medicine, ask your pharmacist about a drug take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking this medicine, as it can increase dizziness and other nervous system side effects. Do not take St. John's Wort (a herbal supplement) — it can lower the levels of this medicine in your blood and make it less effective. Avoid driving, operating heavy machinery, or doing dangerous activities until you know how this medicine affects you, as it can cause dizziness, drowsiness, or difficulty concentrating, especially in the first few weeks. Do not take other HIV medications that contain the same ingredients (such as other medicines with emtricitabine, tenofovir, or efavirenz) unless your doctor tells you to. Tell your doctor and pharmacist about ALL medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take, as many drugs can interact with this medicine, including certain antibiotics, antifungals, cholesterol medicines, blood thinners, and seizure medications.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: signs of a serious allergic reaction (rash, hives, swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, difficulty breathing); signs of liver problems (yellowing of skin or eyes, dark urine, severe stomach pain, nausea or vomiting that won't stop, loss of appetite); signs of kidney problems (decreased urination, swelling in your legs or ankles, unusual tiredness); severe depression, thoughts of suicide, or unusual changes in mood or behavior; severe rash or blistering skin; bone pain or weakness that is new or worsening; signs of lactic acidosis — a rare but serious buildup of acid in the blood — including fast or difficult breathing, stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, feeling cold, dizziness, or irregular heartbeat. Also call your doctor if dizziness, sleep problems, or mood changes do not improve after the first few weeks.
when_it_works: This medicine starts working right away to reduce the amount of HIV in your blood. Most people begin to see their viral load go down within the first few weeks of treatment. However, it may take 3 to 6 months of consistent daily use before the viral load becomes 'undetectable' (so low that standard tests cannot measure it). An undetectable viral load means the medicine is working well and also greatly reduces the risk of passing HIV to others. You may not feel any different at first, but it is still very important to keep taking your medicine every day as prescribed.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Tell your doctor immediately if you are pregnant or plan to become pregnant. This medicine can harm an unborn baby, especially in the first trimester (first 12 weeks). Women of childbearing age must use effective birth control while taking this medicine and for 12 weeks after stopping it. Breastfeeding: Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine. HIV can be passed to a baby through breast milk. Kidney problems: This medicine may not be safe if you have moderate to severe kidney disease. Your doctor may check your kidney function before and during treatment and may switch you to a different medication. Liver problems: Use with caution if you have liver disease, including hepatitis B or C. Your doctor will monitor your liver closely. If you have hepatitis B, do not stop this medicine without talking to your doctor, as your hepatitis B may suddenly get worse. Children: This medicine is only approved for children weighing at least 40 kg (about 88 pounds). The dose for younger or smaller children will be different and decided by your doctor. Older adults: Older adults may be more sensitive to the side effects of this medicine, especially kidney and bone-related effects. Regular monitoring is important.
